objective: For a dual-PC livestream setup (gaming PC -> stream laptop) at 1080p60 where the streaming-PC encoding is INTENTIONAL: research whether NDI could REPLACE the physical HDMI capture card to improve quality at 1080p60, CONDITIONAL on network availability. Assume network MIGHT be wired gigabit Ethernet or WiFi 6 (treat both cases). GOALS: (1) Explain NDI modes: high-bandwidth NDI (1080p60 ~125-180 Mbps, visually near-lossless I-frame-ish), NDI HX/HX2/HX3 (H.264 compressed, ~6-20 Mbps). Compare LIVE quality at 1080p60 across high-bandwidth NDI, NDI HX3, a generic USB3 capture card, and a high-end PCIe capture card. (2) Sender overhead on the gaming PC: OBS NDI plugin 'Main Output' vs NDI Screen Capture HX, CPU and GPU load on the gaming PC compared to the current OBS fullscreen projector + HDMI capture card (the projector is just a small OpenGL render and the capture card eats a free HDMI output). Does NDI meaningfully add CPU/GPU load to the gaming PC relative to the projector+card approach? (3) Network requirements: minimum bandwidth for high-bandwidth NDI at 1080p60, latency behavior, whether WiFi 6 is acceptable or wired gigabit required, switch IGMP snooping / jumbo frame / NIC offload concerns, jitter. (4) Practical setup. CONCLUDE clearly and rank: (a) If wired gigabit Ethernet is available, can high-bandwidth NDI BEAT a generic USB3 capture card at 1080p60 quality? (b) Is NDI HX3 sufficient to beat the generic card? (c) Given the offload is ALREADY achieved via the capture card, is the added complexity of NDI worth it when the user's priority is QUALITY FIRST and minimal gaming-PC overhead? Output a concise markdown brief with concrete numbers and source URLs with a confidence note.
